framework_notes: FastAPI is the primary web framework (score 1.00 >= 0.75 threshold); references/fastapi.md was loaded in addition to references/python.md and references/patterns.md.

Routes are registered via decorators `@<router>.<verb>(...)` on module-level or factory-nested functions (no handler classes), so source extraction keys on decorator-detected handler functions and their parameters, per references/fastapi.md section 6 (no standalone Decorator AST type; getADecorator() returns the decorator func Expr).

Dependency-injected parameters (default value is a Depends(...)/Security(...) call) are excluded from handler-parameter source extraction; they are framework wiring, not client payload. Header/Cookie defaults are kept as client input.
The custom APIRouter (fides/api/api/util/api_router.py) registers each route twice (with and without trailing slash); this only affects reachability, not source shapes.

notes: Extraction rules were derived only from repository evidence and the CWE-918 pass focus; no vulnerability ground truth, CVE descriptions, fix diffs, or pre-located vulnerable lines were consulted (pre-existing root-level analysis artifacts were deliberately not read).

Both extraction queries are plain multi-column select queries (no @kind metadata) for use with `codeql query run` + `codeql bqrs decode`; they are not intended for `codeql database analyze` SARIF output.

CSV column order matches the prior-project convention (calibre-web): node, candidate_type, callable, flow_kind, receiver, moduleHint, arg_index, line, file:line, expression. arg_index is -1 when not applicable.
flow_kind vocabulary: param/return/field/argument as in prior projects.

AST-literal matching (e.g. requests.get by object Name 'requests', httpx.post by object Name 'httpx') is used because CodeQL resolved-API modeling is not guaranteed for every optional dependency; every matched call-site family was individually confirmed against this source tree, and import resolution must be validated during LLM labeling.
urllib.request.urlopen / urlretrieve / aiohttp / http.client are NOT used anywhere in src/ (verified by grep; urllib usage is parse-only) - no candidates and no coverage gap for those APIs.
No file:/data: scheme loading exists in this source tree; nothing extracted for non-HTTP schemes. Local-only file reads are not CWE-918 sinks and are not extracted.
Scope restriction to src/fides/** excludes the nested fides-db CodeQL database directory and all repo-root test/harness trees by construction.

mailchimp transactional dispatcher (message_dispatch_service.py:418) posts to the fixed constant https://mandrillapp.com/api/1.0/messages/send - extracted as a requests sink for completeness, but the URL is a literal; only the payload is config-derived.
mailgun dispatchers (:471/:492/:512) use fixed base URLs with {api_version}/{domain} path segments from MessagingConfig details - the domain does not control the host; labeling should weigh this.

Second-order (response-derived) URLs: pagination_strategy_link.py builds the next request path from a next_link read out of the previous SaaS response (response.links or body); this response-to-URL propagation needs a summary step in Phase 2 if labeling considers it in-scope.

Async hand-off: privacy requests are created via the API and executed in a worker process (request_runner/graph tasks) with data passed through a Redis cache (privacy_request.cache_identity etc.). Source (endpoint body) and sinks (connector execution) therefore live in different call stacks; realistic taint paths require cache/queue summary modeling in Phase 2.

httpx Client.build_request / Request(...).prepare() calls (fides_client.py:96-104, authenticated_client.py:63-69) construct request objects but do not perform network I/O; only the subsequent .send() sites are extracted as sinks.
boto3 S3 storage upload and azure-blob/object-store storage configs (storage_endpoints.py) use object-storage SDKs, not HTTP URL fetches; excluded from CWE-918 sink scope and documented here.
